events.note:
Erwin Zelmer was a German soldier who was killed in action in World War 2 on January 1, 1944. He held the rank of Gefreiter (Private) in 10. Kavallerie-Regiment Nord of the Wehrmacht.

The city of Fellin (modern-day Viljandi) and its vicinity in Estonia was chosen as the place of installation. During the regiment's deployment in the Russian campaign, the city remained its garrison location. Despite the very short formation phase in Fellin - some squadrons had hardly existed for more than 4 weeks - the regiment was ready for war very quickly. Already at the beginning of October 1943, the 1st Cavalry Regiment North was transferred to the Wesenberg area on the north coast of Estonia to secure the oil and slate deposits mined at Kiviölü.

In the first days of November 1943, the II. Abt., which was still being formed, was loaded with the regiment and transferred via Walk - Pleskau to the Ostrow - Palkino area for partisan use in rail transport. The Rgts.Gef.Stand was initially in Palkino, from 01.12. in Slakovichi, in the second half of December in Karamyshevo.

By Christmas 1943, the regiment's squadrons. mainly used to secure the west-east railway connection Pleskau - Staraya Russa in the front line of AOK 16.

The regiment formed the 5th Cavalry Regiment in the summer of 1944.

(from https://www.lexikon-der-wehrmacht.de/Gliederungen/Kavallerieregimenter/KavRNord-R.htm)



The main weight of the defense of the area between Elva and Päidla fell on the 12th Luftwaffe field division, which had been fighting on the northern front in Russia since 1943 and, unlike several other air force field divisions, was a combat-capable unit. The division commander was Major General Gottfried Weber. The division consisted of the 23rd, 24th and 25th Jaeger regiments (2 battalions each), an artillery regiment, a fusilier battalion and other support units. [42] In the division, Estonians fought alongside the Germans, who had been there, for example, from the reserve regiment of the border guard regiments. The division commander, who had already fought in Estonia in 1941, had great sympathy for the Estonians. [43]

Päidla and Nõni initially remained in the offensive sector assigned to the 189th Rifle Division of the Red Army. On August 18, the division commander Pavel Potapov ordered the 880th Rifle Regiment to advance across Sirvaste from Heisri manor on the right wing of the division, pass Valgjärvi on the right and, passing through Saluala and Lutiket, reach the Tatra-Otepää road on Makita. The offensive sector of the 326th rifle division remained to the right from Kodijärve manor, the 891st and 864th rifle regiments were to advance on the left.

(from https://paidel.fandom.com/et/wiki/Teine_maailmas%C3%B5da)
